articles.title: Apple gears up for September iPhone launch with retail employee lottery
articles.summary: With Apple Inc gearing up for its biggest product launch of the year, the company is opening a lottery for US retail employees who want to help staff the in-person unveiling.
articles.content: Stay signed in to save the points you've earned. Click on the points to redeem your rewards at Nexus before they expire. With Apple Inc gearing up for its biggest product launch of the year, the company is opening a lottery for US retail employees who want to help staff the in-person unveiling. The lottery allows retail employees to apply to work the event, where they’ll help organise lines, check in guests, greet attendees, offer directions and support the security teams, according to a memo that was seen by Bloomberg News. The launch event will take place during the first half of September, the company told staff, without providing a more specific date. Historically, Apple’s iPhone presentations have taken place on the second Tuesday or Wednesday of that month. Since Labour Day in the US falls on Monday, Sept 7, a Wednesday event appears slightly more likely, as it would preserve the workday travel window Apple has historically provided for attendees. In the memo, Apple said it was "excited to offer US store team members the opportunity to participate in the Event Support Experience Program.” A spokesperson for the Cupertino, California-based company declined to comment. Apple has relied on retail employees to help staff major product launches for years. Workers who participated in either this year’s Worldwide Developers Conference or last year’s iPhone launch aren’t eligible for the upcoming program. Interested employees must apply by Aug 8, and Apple will notify those selected by Aug 17, according to the memo. This year’s September event carries added significance. It will be the first major product unveiling under Chief Executive Officer John Ternus, who is set to take over from Tim Cook on Sept 1. articles.title: Apple’s New CEO Is Bringing a Familiar Face Back From Retirement. The Shift Is Happening.
articles.summary: Apple’s incoming CEO is already making moves that could hint at the company’s next chapter post-Tim Cook’s era.
articles.content: Apple (AAPL) is about to hand its top position to an engineer, and the early signs suggest the company’s focus may be shifting even more toward its products. John Ternus becomes CEO on September 1, taking over from Tim Cook, who steps into the role of executive chairman. Ternus is not a finance or operations leader like Cook. He has spent his whole career in hardware, having joined Apple’s product design team in 2001 and running its hardware engineering since 2013. His track record is stacked with the products people actually hold. Ternus helped bring the iPad and AirPods to life, and oversaw hardware work across the iPhone, Mac, and Apple Watch. More recently, his teams redefined the iPhone 17 lineup, including the thin iPhone Air, and gave AirPods the ability to work as hearing aids. Even Cook, while announcing the handover, described Ternus as having “ the mind of an engineer, the soul of an innovator .” Now Ternus is building his own team, and his very first hire makes a statement. He is bringing a former vice president of hardware engineering, Laura Legros, out of retirement to report directly to him. Legros is a familiar face to longtime Apple watchers, having introduced the MacBook Air in 2018 and unveiled the iPad Air design in 2020. An engineer taking the top seat and pulling a trusted hardware deputy back in has fueled speculation that Apple’s focus could tilt toward hardware and product innovation. Tim Cook’s record is not one to walk away from. Over his tenure, Apple grew from a roughly $350 billion company to well over $4 trillion, and annual revenue nearly quadrupled to more than $416 billion.
